audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers give Jax four stages (Gnar / Skill / Jax / Jax / Gnar / Jax / Jax). The packet says Gnar / Gnar / Skill / Skill / Skill / Skill / Jax, and the packet matches the page's own whys at all seven rows: whys[1] has Gnar chunking and shoving, whys[2] says 'genuinely a coin-flip', whys[3] 'volatile Rage window', whys[4] 'the level is a wash on Rage timing', whys[5] 'keeps the duel even', whys[6] Jax out-scales. The lane also runs 52.09% for Gnar over 766 games while the page calls it TRICKY at 7.5/10.
audit.why: Jax does not own a stage before two items on this data — the mid-lane stages are Rage-dependent coin flips, which is 'Skill', not a Jax row.
audit.corrected: Chart flipped as one atomic group in both layers to the packet, ratings moved to match, and diff brought to EVEN 6/10 with the tone, difficulty line and rating line in agreement.

audit.why: Four spikes present and real: Lvl 1-2 range window, Lvl 4-5 Rage volatility, Jax's first item, Jax at R plus two items.

audit.whatIsWrong: Counter Strike carries no cooldown and the page never says what it does and does not dodge; Empower is never mentioned at all.
audit.why: Counter Strike is 17/15/13/11/9 and Riot's text says it dodges incoming ATTACKS — so Boomerang, Wallop and GNAR! all land through a raised E, which is the single most useful thing a kiting Gnar can know here. Empower is 5s at rank 3 and is an attack reset, so the wind-up rather than the cast is the cue to step out of his Q range.
audit.corrected: 13s-at-rank-3 and the attacks-only rule written into the do's, cooldown block and Key Ability Interactions; Empower named with its 5s reset in the cooldown block and wants.foe[1].
sources: enemyKit Jax E cd 17/15/13/11/9 and text
enemyKit Jax W cd 7/6/5/4/3 and autoReset flag
